mismatch.message: unsupported hero command: wiz_where() for the extended command 'wizwhere' is not ported

summary: The first remaining stop is wizwhere at 1650, with no earlier screen, cursor or RNG difference. C wiz_where calls the non-menu print_dungeon path; JavaScript currently implements only the level-teleport menu. The read.c creation family now accepts source-defined state, gender and disposition modifiers, but hidden/invisible creation recordings still require the missing flash_glyph_at animation.

source.branch: C wizcmds.c wiz_where218–225 calls print_dungeon(FALSE) in wizard mode, otherwise prints the unavailable-command message, and returns ECMD_OK. The command registry names wiz_where but its JavaScript dispatcher has no implementation.
callers: extcmdlist_data.js maps wizwhere to wiz_where; the extended-command dispatcher reaches its unsupported-command boundary. C cmd.c uses the same command registry entry and wizcmds.c owns the implementation.

The required output is dungeon.c print_dungeon2290–2440, which creates NHW_MENU, emits dungeon/branch/special-level lines with putstr, adds floating branches and invocation or portal coordinates, then displays and destroys the window.
dependencies: Complete both bymenu branches of whole dungeon.c print_dungeon and print_branch while retaining the existing level-teleport caller. The non-menu branch does not filter dungeons by the hero being in the endgame, does not use selection letters, and uses a blank branch prefix even when the hero is there.

Preserve source order of dungeon headings, branches before and after each special level, the stronghold tune, and floating branches. Invocation position takes precedence over portal reporting; absent-portal text appears only on the C-listed portal-bearing levels.

The hitmu port now clears hidden state, uses the exact canonical display.c tp_sensemon predicate, preserves naming/output/redraw order and implements the permanent HP-loss reader. Ordinary production hit recordings already exist; hidden-attacker and nonzero permanent-loss entry recordings remain open because setup and the AD_DETH writer are incomplete.

Accepted mfind0 and Warning wiring now preserve marker memory, coordinate-aware messages, acknowledgement before reveal and source return values. Canonical dmonsfree runs on the planning clone after the monster scan before allmain movement allocation; the previous allocation failure is resolved.

Whole goto_level and its supporting cleanup owners are implemented, including the Mines achievement and terminal punishment-ball and fall damage guards. Two independent Minetown level-teleport recordings match; they do not establish trapdoor, portal, endgame, tutorial, terminal or other exceptional entry coverage.

mon.c minliquid/minliquid_core and supporting split_mon/cloneu/clone_mon are implemented with source-ordered HP, RNG, death and planning output. Liquid-specific entry recordings, exceptional partial rloc routes and other source callers remain open; trap.c inventory chain calls and mon.c deal_with_overcrowding remain named discarded-call gaps.

Separate unresolved coverage: make_stoned/minstapetrify/do_stone_mon stoning gaps; unrecorded hero/monster stoning directions, corpse-weapon entry and attack-triggered stone-golem conversion; passive cold/fire/electricity/paralysis and lethal/recovery families; eating/non-food cleanup; skinback artifact-light radius and rare armor/Eyes-of-the-Overworld cleanup.

The whole read.c cant_revive/create_particular_parse/create_particular_creation/create_particular family is now implemented. Sleeping and peaceful creation have independent matching recordings. Hidden-attacker witnesses still need eligible placement on objects or water where required, actual hidden state and an executed hitmu; plain or qualified creation alone does not establish the hit entry.

Hidden/invisible creation has a further source dependency after read.c parses and applies the modifiers: read.c3346–3347 calls mon.c flash_mon6067–6081 for an unspotted creation. Its JavaScript owner preserves temporary vision and display-RNG evaluation but records display.c flash_glyph_at as unported. Matching the hidden-creation animation remains necessary for that independent recording; ordinary sleeping or peaceful creation does not establish it.

The flash_mon completion must also use C mon_to_glyph rather than map_monster_glyph_info: the latter selects a pet glyph for tame monsters and a detected glyph for mlet zero. Preserve the ordinary monster glyph and display-RNG order, and prevent the global newsym tail from painting live state when called with a planning clone.

evidence: .cache/A34-development-scan.json and .cache/A34-queue.json locate the wizwhere stop at 1650. The earlier combined focused replay run-lpgqS9 likewise emitted 1650 screens with divergence:null.

Source comparison traced wizcmds.c wiz_where and the full dungeon.c print_dungeon/print_branch bodies. JavaScript dungeon.js currently supports only bymenu TRUE; its former NHW_TEXT description of the absent branch is inaccurate because C creates NHW_MENU for both modes.

The existing marilith and yellow-mold production recordings contain hitmu RNG calls and cover ordinary hit resolution. The abandoned plain-eel probes contained no hitmu or mattacku calls; retained hidden/hostile recipes are planned inputs and establish no entry coverage yet.

Supporting potion.c split_mon, mhitu.c cloneu and makemon.c clone_mon now own splitting, runtime clone creation, planning RNG, shopkeeper naming and the C struct-copy fields including mw, EMIN.parentmid and the EDOG goal coordinate. mhitu passiveum, trap rust effects and uhitm pudding splitting use the canonical helpers. Initialized focused checks establish runtime creation and planning isolation; no new liquid-branch production recording is claimed.

Existing achievement display recordings cover Bell and Candelabrum rows; final disclosure, ascension, relinquished-object wording and female-rank production routes remain open. The liquid functions have ordinary movement caller evidence in bee-eats-royal-jelly-span, but dedicated liquid, swap, fountain and zero-speed distress recordings remain open.

Source comparison of mon.c flash_mon and js/mon.js flash_mon confirms that the temporary display.c flash_glyph_at call is still skipped via note_unported. The read.c hidden/invisible caller retains this dependency after its parser refusal was removed.

The combined checkpoint at 6c085eb2 preserves the first wizwhere stop and verifies two independent read.c creations: sleeping newt and peaceful newt. Source comparison covers the full parser, species replacement, gender conflict flags, post-creation state and bounded retry message; UnsupportedMonsterRequestError was removed. Hidden creation still reaches the separately recorded flash_glyph_at gap.

Direct source comparison: mon.c flash_mon calls mon_to_glyph unconditionally, while js/display.js map_monster_glyph_info chooses Boolean(monster.mtame) and an mlet-zero detected arm. js/mon.js flash_mon also calls global display.newsym after operating on its supplied state; the animation completion must preserve planning isolation through that tail.
